Outlet: Bank of England, Monetary Policy Summary, meeting ending 4 November 2026 (published Thursday 5 November 2026)
Bank Rate increased to 4% - November 2026 Monetary Policy Summary and Minutes

At its meeting ending on 4 November 2026, the Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) voted by a majority of 8-1 to increase Bank Rate by 0.25 percentage points, to 4%. One member voted to increase Bank Rate by 0.5 percentage points, to 4.25%.

"UK CPI inflation increased to 3.5% in September. It is now expected to rise to around 5% by the middle of next year."
Staff projected "headline CPI inflation to reach around 4½% in 2027 Q1" and "around 5% in 2027 Q2".

The conflict in the Middle East is now in its ninth month. Global energy prices have continued to rise from an already elevated level. While the direct effects of higher energy prices are clear, and will continue to feed into firm and household energy bills, there remains "limited evidence of knock-on effects on other prices and wages." "The degree of inflationary pressure in the pipeline is now sufficient to warrant an increase in Bank Rate." Activity data in recent months have generally been stronger than expected, adding to the case for modestly tighter monetary policy.

"Monetary policy is not on a pre-set path." The Committee will continue to assess the evidence at each meeting, in particular "how likely high energy prices are to feed through to other prices and the economy more broadly, by monitoring the evolution of underlying pay, pricing behaviour, and slack." The Committee will adjust Bank Rate as necessary to ensure CPI inflation returns to the 2% target in the medium term.
